subject: Pediatrics
subtopic: Clinical picture, diagnosis, treatment and prognosis
concept: Pediatric bleeding disorders arise from platelet number/function abnormalities, von Willebrand factor defects, coagulation factor deficiencies or acquired consumption.

content.definition: A bleeding disorder is impaired primary or secondary hemostasis causing abnormal bleeding after injury or spontaneously.
content.explanation: Mucocutaneous bleeding such as epistaxis, gum bleeding and petechiae suggests platelet or von Willebrand-related disease. Deep tissue bleeding, hemarthroses and delayed post-procedural bleeding suggest coagulation-factor deficiency such as hemophilia. DIC is an acquired consumptive process.
content.mechanism: Primary hemostasis depends on platelets and vWF. Secondary hemostasis generates thrombin and fibrin through coagulation factors.
content.clinical_relevance: Bleeding phenotype guides the differential but does not replace laboratory confirmation. Pediatric diagnosis should include family history and medication review before invasive procedures.
content.diagnosis: Initial assessment includes bleeding history, family history, CBC with platelet count, PT/INR and aPTT. Hemophilia requires factor VIII/IX assays. VWD evaluation uses VWF antigen, VWF activity and factor VIII; repeat testing may be necessary.
content.treatment: Treatment is cause- and severity-specific. Hemophilia may require factor replacement or appropriate non-factor therapy. Selected VWD patients may respond to desmopressin, while VWF-containing therapy is used when indicated. Severe platelet bleeding may require platelet support. DIC requires urgent treatment of the underlying cause plus supportive hemostatic management when clinically indicated.
high_yield: Mucocutaneous bleeding suggests platelet/vWF dysfunction; hemarthrosis suggests coagulation-factor deficiency.
Hemophilia A is factor VIII deficiency; hemophilia B is factor IX deficiency.
VWD can have normal routine screening tests, so specific VWF testing is required.
Factor assays establish hemophilia type and severity.
Interpret laboratory results in clinical context and repeat when appropriate.
